Test Bowler Match Factor

Compare Test bowlers by how their average compares with the other bowlers in the same matches, instead of raw averages alone. Every setting from the Excel model is here: innings or date ranges, minimum wickets, home and away, opposition, same-type comparisons, and the peak-run finder.

Unpacking 37,984 bowling innings…

Click a bowler for a profile with rolling form, opposition and home or away splits. Match factor is shown as 1 minus (bowler average divided by the comparison average), so 30% means a bowling average 30% lower than the comparison group. Blank cells mean the bowler is below the minimum, or has no wickets in that slice.

Slides a window of consecutive career innings across each bowler's career, finds the window with the highest match factor and reports it. Home and away is always All here, as in the Excel macro.

The idea

A bowling average depends on the era, the pitches and the opposition. Match factor asks a narrower question: how good was this bowler's average compared with the other bowlers who bowled in the same matches?

For each bowler the model adds up his runs and wickets, adds up the runs and wickets of the comparison group in the same innings, and reports 1 − (bowler average ÷ comparison average). A bowler averaging 20 in matches where the others averaged 30 scores 33%.

Comparison groups

ColumnCompared with
Total matchEvery other bowler in the same innings, both teams, pace and spin.
Type onlyOther bowlers of the same type (pace against pace, spin against spin).
Type only - oppositionSame-type bowlers on the opposing team only. Removes the effect of having a great bowling partner.
Type only - same teamSame-type bowlers on his own team. Shows who carried his side. Teammates must have bowled at least the chosen share of his balls.

Settings, as in the workbook

SettingWhat it does
Innings between / DateLimit each bowler to his Nth to Mth career innings, or to matches within a date range (for example a decade).
Min wicketsBowlers with fewer wickets in the selected slice are left out. Judged on all opposition, even when a single team is selected.
Home / AwayOnly matches in the bowler's own country, only matches away, or all.
TeamOnly innings against one opposition. The minimum wickets still applies to the bowler's overall total.
Peak finderThe workbook macro. It slides a window of consecutive innings along each career and keeps the best match factor. As in the macro, a duration of 50 covers the starting innings and the 50 after it, 51 innings in all.

Notes on the data

  • Tests from January 1970 to August 2026, taken from ESPNcricinfo Statsguru. The model lists 1,390 bowlers.
  • Overs before 1980 are converted to balls using 8-ball overs where applicable.
  • Everything on this page is calculated in your browser from the same per-innings data as the spreadsheet, and the results match the workbook's saved values.
